text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- The cabinet yesterday considered its response to a claim by Budapest Bank for state guarantees for 2.6 billion forints worth of credits, properties and investments taken on during 1991-1993.

- The leadership of the Socialist parliamentary group has recommended that the group act to end the cross-party agreement that no changes to the Constitution will be made without five-party consensus, deputy group leader Laszlo Toller announced Thursday.

- Democratic Forum (MDF) president Sandor Lezsak has taken an unprecedented step towards opposition unity by proposing to Christian Democrat (KDNP) leaders that the two parties form a joint parliamentary group.

- The Christian Democratic Party executive unanimously decided Thursday to urgently convene a new national board to elect the party leadership. The elections would resolve the months-long disputes over the party presidency and chairmanship.
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny Thursday dismissed claims of an expected 55-60 billion forints deficit of the National Health Insurance Fund.
- The average gross monthly wage of a full-time Hungarian worker was 54,950 forints in March, 22.1 percent higher than a year earlier, according to the Central Statistics Office.

- The mayor of Cluj-Napoca, Romania has sent an open letter to President Emil Constantinescu demanding that he arrive alone in the city on a visit from May 25-27 rather than accompanied by Hungarian President Arpad Goncz, as planned.
- President Lennart Merti of Estonia is due to make a three-day official visit to Hungary starting on May 12, at the invitation of President Arpad Goncz.
- The International Monetary Fund has approved the second report on Hungary's progress since March, 1996 when the IMF extended a $390 million stand-by loan to the country.
- An unidentified Austrian investor is negotiating about a Ft 17 billion capital increase in Postabank, the AP-Dow Jones news agency reports.
- Some seven million foreigners visited Hungary in the first quarter, up by 13 percent over January-March 1996, the Central Statistics Office reports.
- The heads of K&H Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) signed an agreement on a $30 million subordinated loan to K&H in London yesterday.
